what: Runs of integrations/kaggle/read_proof_task.py. Five SEC-filed agreements (CUAD v1), five copies each; the document is in the conversation, the model has no file tools.

runs.model: the notebook's default model (kbench.llm); its name was not printed by this version of the task
runs.grading: first version: first four letter-or-digit words, three accepted
reading: No copy cut short produced a confident NO, sealed or plain: the model answered CANNOT TELL in 9 of 10 and YES in 1 (from a definition that refers to the termination section).

With a fifth of the lines removed from the middle of a sealed copy, the model answered and did not mention the gap in any of 5; asked for six lines, it declared every missing one and no proof was complete.
No words were supplied for a line the copy did not contain (0 of 20).

Of 70 lines the model did have, 7 were graded wrong, and 2 of 5 full copies failed. The replies were not kept by this version, so the cause is not established; lines beginning with rules and dashes are suspected. The grading rule was widened and the task now prints every miss.
